chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Teddy Hill's band at the Savoy
summary: Teddy Hill's band, second only to Webb's, had Dillard, Collins, Eldridge, Dickie Wells, Procope, Chu Berry and a high-playing brass section.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And then Teddy Hill had a fantastic band up there, too.
: Oh, he played the Savoy, too?
Oh, sure, he was one of the main bands in the Savoy, like he was second to Chick Webb.
What a band he had. He had -- his trumpets was Bill Dillard, Shad Collins, and Roy Eldridge.
And Dickie Wells on trombone. Saxophones was Howard Johnson and Russell Procope and --
Yeah, two altos. -- and Choo Berry was the tenor. And Sam Allen was the pianist and old man Fulbright -- I forget his first name -- he was the bass player.
He used to wear all them funny hats.
That's right. And I think the guitar player was named Bobby Johnson, too. And Bill Beason was the drummer.
Bill Beason later was with the Kirby band.
Oh, is that so. Beason -- Okay.
Bill Beason came after O'Neill Spencer.
Oh, I see. That's what I was checking, checking up.
Let's see, O'Neill Spencer was at --
That band was the most fantastic band. It was a beautiful band, Teddy Hill. And the trumpets, they could play so high, all of them, and Dickie Wells played right up high with them.
And Bill Dillard was a wonderful vocalist. Bill Dillard turned out to be a singer later on.
I think he's been with numerous choirs and he's been with some Broadway shows, too.
Yes, and he is one of those guys that stayed in the YMCA and he kept his body --
